name: Little Soul Cafe
mission: Take a seat near the handmade counter and follow a record from its first track. Ask for the artist's name when there is a natural pause.
doorNotes: Taisei Building, second floor. Opens at 19:00.

name: Bookshop B&B
mission: Browse one shelf outside your usual subject. Choose a book by its first page, and take the title into the rest of the walk.
doorNotes: Browsing does not require buying a drink. Talks require a separate reservation.

name: Bear Pond Espresso
mission: Start at the espresso counter. Ask what is being served today and keep the first drink short enough to leave time for the streets outside.

name: Reload
mission: Walk the small courtyards and look for one independent shop or display that would disappear inside a department store.

name: BIG LOVE RECORDS
mission: Head for a label or artist you do not recognise. Ask which new arrival the staff would keep for themselves.

name: NAT RECORDS
mission: Look for the independent label behind a punk or garage record. Follow that label to another band instead of shopping by fame.
doorNotes: Kitazawa 2-10-10, FI Kyodo Building, fourth floor. This is the relocated Shimokitazawa shop.

name: Record Shop BASE
mission: Find a small-label release and read the insert if a browsing copy is available. Look for the scene around the band.

name: Record Boy
mission: Compare one heavy record from Japan with one from elsewhere. Look for what the artwork and label tell you before asking for a recommendation.

name: Face Records Shibuya
mission: Give the jazz or soul section fifteen focused minutes. Leave with one unfamiliar musician's name even if you leave the record in its sleeve.
doorNotes: Udagawacho 10-2, third floor. Record Store Day lists shop hours as 13:00–19:00.

name: ELLA RECORDS
mission: Look for one Japanese pressing and compare its sleeve and credits with a release you already know.

name: Lighthouse Records
mission: Choose a dance record by the label rather than the headliner. Ask where that sound sits in the shop's current selection.

name: Manhattan Records
mission: Read the production credits on a hip-hop release. Find one collaborator whose name is new to you.

name: Waltz
mission: Go to the cassette shelf first. Pick a format you usually stream past and read the small print on its label.

name: Organic Music
mission: Find a record filed somewhere you do not normally browse. Use the sleeve notes to decide which sound to follow next.

name: Record Station
mission: Browse a small run of records slowly. Compare the original release date with what the sleeve makes you expect.

name: Universounds
mission: Look for a Japanese jazz release and trace one musician through the credits to another recording.

name: Pianola Records
mission: Choose a record whose description makes you hesitate. Let that uncertainty be the point of the stop.

name: Dub Store Records
mission: Find a seven-inch and read the producer and studio credits. Follow the rhythm beyond the singer on the label.

name: Coconuts Disk Kichijoji
mission: Choose one record from the shop's own recommendations before searching for a title you came in knowing.

name: Coconuts Disk Ekoda
mission: Find a record at the boundary between two genres. Read the shop's note and decide which part you want to hear first.

name: Bar Music
mission: Settle in for the selection rather than asking for a favourite immediately. Keep one track name for the walk home.
doorNotes: Dogenzaka 1-6-7, fifth floor. Opens at 18:00; irregular days off.

name: Alfie
mission: Use the published lineup to choose one musician you do not know. Give the room enough time for a whole set.

name: Shinjuku PIT INN
mission: Choose a show from the official programme and arrive for its door time. Follow the least familiar name in the lineup.

name: The Room
mission: Check the selector and entry time for the night. Follow a transition between two records rather than waiting for a song you know.

name: Forestlimit
mission: Choose a dated event from the programme. Give the unfamiliar act in the lineup your attention before deciding what scene this is.

name: SPREAD
mission: Read the night's lineup and door time first. Stay for one act you cannot place by name alone.

name: Bonobo
mission: Choose the night by its posted selectors. Listen for one transition that changes the mood of the room.

name: Bookshop Title
mission: Read the first page of a book outside your usual shelf. Choose one sentence to carry into the next stop.

name: UTRECHT
mission: Find an artist's book whose form changes how you read it. Spend time with its paper, binding or sequence of images.

name: POST
mission: Follow the publisher being presented rather than starting with an artist you know. Look for a visual idea repeated across different books.

name: Flying Books
mission: Take the stairs and browse one narrow subject slowly. Look for a publication that could not work as a feed post.

name: SHIBUYA PUBLISHING & BOOKSELLERS
mission: Find a book from a publisher you have never followed. Notice how its cover and typography frame the subject.

name: Sunny Boy Books
mission: Choose a slim book you could finish in a sitting. Ask what has arrived from a small publisher recently.

name: Kosho Horo
mission: Browse across subjects rather than following one alphabet. Find a book that connects something you read with something you listen to.

name: tata bookshop/gallery
mission: Find a book you would rarely see in a general bookshop. Look for what its maker did with the page itself.

name: Fugensha
mission: Follow a photographer through the books rather than searching for one famous image. Notice how a full sequence changes your reading.

name: Bohemian's Guild
mission: Compare an older art publication with a contemporary one. Look for an idea that outlasted its original design.

name: Yamada Shoten
mission: Spend time with a print or illustrated book. Look closely at the marks that a small screen usually hides.

name: Komiyama Tokyo
mission: Choose a photobook from a decade you rarely browse. Notice what its images assume about the person looking at them.

name: Magnif
mission: Pick an old magazine by its cover date. Find one detail that feels unexpectedly current.

name: Isseido Booksellers
mission: Look at a book as a physical object. Find a binding, map or illustration worth seeing at its original size.

name: Ohya Shobo
mission: Look for a map or printed image of an older city. Compare one street or landmark with the Tokyo outside.

name: GA Bookshop
mission: Follow one building through its drawings and photographs. Look for the detail that explains how it meets the street.

name: Sanyodo Book Store
mission: Browse the ground-floor books and notice how the gallery and cafe extend the same visit upstairs.

name: Mograg Gallery
mission: Choose one work from the current show and inspect its smallest repeated detail. Keep the artist's name rather than collecting every image.

name: Taka Ishii Gallery
mission: Use the current exhibition to follow one artist beyond a single work. Notice what changes as you move across the room.

name: SCAI THE BATHHOUSE
mission: Look at where the old building ends and the exhibition begins. Choose one work that changes how you see the room.

name: KAYOKOYUKI
mission: Stay with one work before reading the explanation. Compare what you first noticed with what the artist's text asks you to notice.

name: TALION GALLERY
mission: Look for one material or gesture that repeats through the show. Follow it across several works before moving on.

name: MISAKO & ROSEN
mission: Read one artist's name and then look across the whole show. Find a visual decision that belongs to that artist.

name: KANA KAWANISHI GALLERY
mission: Compare the surface of a photographic work with the scene it represents. Notice what only becomes visible in person.

name: WAITINGROOM
mission: Follow one small detail through the current exhibition. Ask how it changes when it appears in another work.

name: Maki Fine Arts
mission: Take a second look at the work you initially walked past. Find one decision in its colour, scale or placement that you missed.

name: Satoko Oe Contemporary
mission: Look at the spaces between works as well as the works themselves. Notice how the exhibition changes your pace.

name: Take Ninagawa
mission: Find a work that makes ordinary material look unfamiliar. Spend a few minutes deciding what caused the change.

name: TARO NASU
mission: Read a title, return to the work and see what the title changes. Keep the question rather than forcing an immediate answer.

name: Ota Fine Arts
mission: Choose one artist you have not followed before. Look for the connection between two works in the current show.

name: HAGISO
mission: Take a break in the reused building and notice one detail of how the space has been kept in use. Then look at what is on display.

name: WISH LESS
mission: Look for the link between the exhibition and the small editions around it. Follow one artist through both formats.

name: GALLERY CONCEAL SHIBUYA
mission: Take the stairs and choose one work to see twice, once before and once after reading the artist's text.

name: WATARI-UM
mission: Follow one idea through the current exhibition and into its printed material. Keep a question to take back into the street.

name: 21_21 DESIGN SIGHT
mission: Choose one ordinary object being reconsidered in the current show. Notice what its display asks you to see differently.

name: GALLERY COMMUNE
mission: Look for an edition or small publication alongside the show. Compare the same artist's work on a wall and on a page.

name: Cafe Bach
mission: Choose a coffee by the question you want answered, such as roast or origin. Notice what changes as the cup cools.

name: GLITCH COFFEE Jimbocho
mission: Choose one origin you do not normally drink. Keep the tasting note that matches your own experience, not the one you think you should find.

name: LEAVES COFFEE ROASTERS
mission: Ask which coffee best shows what the roastery is interested in now. Follow how the first sip differs from the last.

name: KOFFEE MAMEYA
mission: Tell the staff how you usually drink coffee and try the next step they suggest. Treat the conversation as part of the visit.

name: Fuglen Tokyo
mission: Look at one piece of design while you drink. Notice how it works as part of a room rather than as an isolated object.

name: Cafe de l'Ambre
mission: Take time over one coffee and notice its changing temperature. Let a small, deliberate drink interrupt the shopping streets outside.

name: ONIBUS COFFEE Nakameguro
mission: Use the coffee stop to watch how the shop meets the neighbourhood. Keep one small detail from the street, not just the cup.

name: ARiSE COFFEE ROASTERS
mission: Ask about one origin that is new to you. Use the answer to decide the cup rather than choosing from habit.

name: iki ESPRESSO
mission: Pause before the next gallery. Notice one detail of the surrounding streets that would never appear on a museum wall.

name: Dandelion Chocolate Kuramae
mission: Compare the idea of origin in chocolate with origin in coffee. Choose one flavour you can identify without reading its description.

name: Pelican Cafe
mission: Make the bread the focus of the stop. Compare crust, texture and the way a simple serving changes your pace.

name: MIA MIA
mission: Take a coffee break that leaves room for a conversation. Notice how the cafe connects to the street around it.

name: BEEP Akihabara
mission: Read the labels on one piece of older game hardware. Look for a design constraint that explains how people played with it.

name: Super Potato Akihabara
mission: Choose one game you remember and one you have never seen. Compare the controls or packaging before looking at the price.

name: HEY Akihabara
mission: Choose a cabinet by what is happening on screen rather than by the title. Watch someone play, then try to understand one rule yourself.

name: Mandarake Nakano
mission: Pick one narrowly specialised room and inspect the labels. Look for a corner of collecting you did not know had a name.

name: ROBOTROBOT
mission: Find one toy from a world you know and one from a world you do not. Notice what their packaging assumes about the collector.

name: Yamashiroya
mission: Compare two versions of the same kind of toy. Look for the small change that turns a familiar character into a collector's object.

name: THE MUSIC BAR CAVE SHIBUYA
mission: Take the sound system as the main attraction. Pick one element in the mix and follow it through the next record.

name: Onn. Good Track Lounge
mission: Settle in with the selectors' choice and notice how a familiar instrument changes through the room's sound system.
doorNotes: Second floor. ¥1,000 music charge per person plus 20% service; drinks extra.

name: ShugoArts
mission: Compare the first and last works you see. Look for the change in attention the exhibition asks of you.

name: Tomio Koyama Gallery
mission: Choose a work that repays a second look. Notice what its scale does that a reproduced image would not.

name: Mizuma Art Gallery
mission: Look at how an artist builds a world through repeated details. Find the one detail you would use to describe that world to a friend.

name: Tokyo Gallery + BTAP
mission: Choose one artist you do not already follow. Notice how the current show connects a local room to a wider artistic conversation.

name: Art Front Gallery
mission: Find a work that changes your sense of space. Carry that shift in scale back out to the street.

name: Yutaka Kikutake Gallery
mission: Look for a small formal decision that runs through the show. Follow it through more than one work.

name: KOTARO NUKAGA
mission: Look for a work that uses a familiar visual language in an unfamiliar way. Notice what changes when you stand in front of it.

name: GINZA GEKKOSO
mission: Look at the tools and the work together. Find one material that makes you want to make something rather than only look.

name: Spincoaster Music Bar
mission: Choose one unfamiliar artist from the night's selection. Keep the track name and listen again after the walk.

name: Bunkitsu Roppongi
mission: Choose a book from a shelf you normally walk past. Take it into the reading area and give the opening chapter your full attention.
doorNotes: The reading area has an admission fee. Check the current rate before entering.

name: Hi-Fi Record Store
mission: Choose one record for its arrangement or players rather than its headline name. Use the credits as a map to another record.

name: HMV record shop Shibuya
mission: Choose one older Japanese release and compare it with a reissue. Look for a detail in the sleeve or credits that changes your choice.

name: Kanda Brazil
mission: Start with a coffee before the book streets. Look for one detail of the room that makes you slow your browsing pace.

name: Tokyo Opera City Art Gallery
mission: Follow one artist through the current exhibition. Compare the work's original size with what you expected from its reproduction.

name: NTT InterCommunication Center
mission: Choose one work that uses time, sound or participation. Stay with it long enough to notice what changes.

name: Daikanyama T-Site
mission: Choose one cultural subject and follow it across a book, a magazine and a related display. Keep the least obvious connection.

name: GALLERY TARGET
mission: Look for the marks that distinguish the artist from their influences. Choose one detail you could recognise again without a label.
